(4 comments)

The code looks good to me. I checked these points:
- Teardown: osc_device_fini() removes the debugfs and sysfs files and invalidates the import before lprocfs_cli_jobstats_fini(). So no reader, no enable_job_stats store, and no BRW completion can reach the stats after fini.
- Iterator references: start() and next() take one job reference and next()/stop() drop it. The SEQ_START_TOKEN header holds no reference. After seq_file grows its buffer, start(*pos) finds the same job again, so the header is not lost.
- Named removal and expiry both use test_and_set_bit(JS_EXPIRED), so only one of them drops the tree reference.
- When the client retry limit is reached, the new job is not in either tree. Its job_putref() takes the same path as the existing "collision, discard this job" case, so the purge is safe.
- The server path is not changed: proc fops, OJS_HEADER, the seq_write puts, and expiry on release.
- The clock sources match: rq_sent_ns, rq_queued_time_ns and done_time all use ktime_get_real().

I have one question and a few optional points inline.

commit.message:
LU-21060 osc: add OSC job statistics

- Managed Lustre users cannot read server jobstats.  Add per-job OSC
  counters on the client, with no server or wire change.  Collection
  is off by default.
- Add osc.*.enable_job_stats, osc.*.job_stats and
  osc.*.job_cleanup_interval.  job_stats is a root-only debugfs file
  with the server YAML format; job IDs, removal and expiry work as on
  the servers.
- Keep the stats in client_obd.  after_reply() calls a per-device
  callback for successful replies, and ptlrpc_jobstats_log() counts
  them under the job ID of the request.
- Count OST operations by their obdfilter names, and the BRW payload
  bytes really transferred with round-trip and ptlrpcd queue time.
- Client output has its own header record, so seq_file can retry a
  large record.  A complete read expires idle jobs.  A named removal
  claims expiry first, so concurrent clears drop one reference only.
- Limit client insertion retries, so concurrent expiry cannot keep an
  I/O in the accounting path.
- Add man pages, point lljobstat(8) to them, and add sanity tests
  205q, 205r, 205v, 205x and 205z.
